summary.text: A 62-year-old man (173 cm, 64 kg) was scheduled for clipping of an unruptured anterior communicating cerebral artery aneurysm via craniotomy. He had previously received telmisartan and sodium valproate for hypertension and symptomatic epilepsy after a cranial hematoma from right occipital lobe bleeding. Preoperative 12-lead ECG and laboratory tests included serum sodium 141 mEq/L and potassium 4.1 mEq/L. On arrival in the operating room his hemodynamic state was stable.

Anesthesia was induced with propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium and maintained with sevoflurane and remifentanil. Mannitol 200 mL of 20% was given intravenously over 60 min starting 25 min after surgical incision. Approximately 20 min after the end of mannitol, ventricular tachycardia occurred without any preceding ECG change, and blood pressure decreased to below 40 mmHg. Chest compression was started immediately and VT recovered to sinus rhythm at 75 beats/min.

After recovery of sinus rhythm the ECG showed peaked T waves that disappeared after 2 min, and potassium was 6.4 mEq/L with arterial pH 7.43. Calcium gluconate, furosemide and insulin with glucose were administered; potassium was 3.2 mEq/L after 60 min and 3.5 mEq/L at the end of surgery. The clipping was completed without further cardiac instability, the patient was extubated, and no further postoperative event occurred.
